shots.text: Nike paid thirty-five dollars for its logo.
Yes, the Swoosh. The one on every shoe.
It was nineteen seventy-one. Phil Knight ran a small Oregon shoe company, and he needed a logo.
He turned to Carolyn Davidson, a design student at Portland State.
She sent him an invoice. Thirty-five dollars.
He looked at her design and said, I don't love it, but it will grow on me.
He paid. And the Swoosh went onto shoes that same year.
The little company became Nike, a global giant.
Twelve years later, in nineteen eighty-three, Nike thanked her.
A gold Swoosh ring with a diamond. And Nike stock.
One sketch, thirty-five dollars at first, then a ring and shares.
A great idea can look cheap on day one.
